modules.name: autologon
modules.description: Sign in without typing a password (pairs with `username`). XML snippet; cleartext password.
modules.why: Skips the password prompt at every boot — handy for a home PC or a VM you reboot often.
modules.riskNote: Stores the password in the registry in clear text. Don't use it on a shared or portable machine.
modules.content:
<!-- ============================================================================
     InDows module: autologon
     Signs the account in automatically at boot, without typing the password. Pairs with the
     'username' module (same account).

     WHERE: settings pass="oobeSystem" > component "Microsoft-Windows-Shell-Setup"
     ANCHOR (a comment in the base) named:   [InDows:module] account

     REPLACE: __USERNAME__ (the account) and __PASSWORD__ (its password; empty value if no password).
     PERMANENT auto-logon as written. For a ONE-TIME auto-logon, add <LogonCount>1</LogonCount>.

     SECURITY: the password is stored in CLEAR TEXT in autounattend.xml. Never commit a real password
     to a public repo. Auto-logon also means anyone who powers on the PC is logged in as you.
     ============================================================================ -->
<AutoLogon>
    <Username>__USERNAME__</Username>
    <Enabled>true</Enabled>
    <Password>
        <Value>__PASSWORD__</Value>
        <PlainText>true</PlainText>
    </Password>
</AutoLogon>

params.label: Account name (same as the account you sign in as)
Password (leave blank for none; stored in clear text)

modules.name: computer-name

modules.why: Names the PC for you, so you don't type it during setup and it stays consistent on the network.
modules.riskNote: Cosmetic and reversible. Just avoid characters Windows rejects (spaces, most symbols).
modules.content:
<!-- ============================================================================
     InDows module: computer-name
     Sets the PC name automatically. Without this module Windows assigns a random
     name (e.g. DESKTOP-AB12CD3) which you can change later in Settings.

     WHERE: settings pass="specialize" > component "Microsoft-Windows-Shell-Setup"
     ANCHOR (a comment in the base) named:   [InDows:module] specialize-shell-setup

<ComputerName>__COMPUTERNAME__</ComputerName>

modules.name: context-menu
modules.description: Restore the Windows 10 classic right-click menu (removes "Show more options"). reg [U] CLSID `InprocServer32`.
modules.why: Brings back the full Windows 10 right-click menu, so every action is one click instead of hidden behind "Show more options".
modules.riskNote: Purely a shell preference. Revert by deleting one registry key.
modules.content:
# InDows module: context-menu
# Restores the Windows 10 classic right-click menu (no "Show more options" extra click).
# Anchor: [InDows:module] default-user-scripts
# Mechanism: register an EMPTY InprocServer32 for the Win11 menu CLSID, which disables it.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-context-menu.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }

$key = 'Registry::HKEY_USERS\DefaultUser\Software\Classes\CLSID\{86ca1aa0-34aa-4e8b-a509-50c905bae2a2}\InprocServer32'

Log '=== context-menu start ==='
New-Item -Path $key -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
# Set the key's (Default) value to an EMPTY string (this is what disables the new menu).
Set-Item -Path $key -Value '' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Log '=== context-menu done ==='

modules.name: debloat-appx
modules.description: Remove preinstalled Store apps (provisioned + per-user) so new users don't get them.
modules.why: Removes preinstalled Store apps you don't want — tick them one by one (the safe, low-regret ones are pre-ticked).
modules.riskNote: Each app is an individual choice, on top of the base. NOTE: the InDows base already removes a fixed set of Store apps unconditionally, so for those, un-ticking here will NOT bring them back. The Xbox app is the Game Pass client (keep it if you play Game Pass); the Clock app holds alarms, timers and Focus Sessions — both start unticked. Mail & Calendar and People are already retired by Microsoft.
modules.content:
# InDows module: debloat-appx
# Removes preinstalled Store apps. Each line below removes ONE app; the InDows GUI ticks/unticks them
# individually (a commented line is kept). Removing a provisioned package stops NEW users getting it too.
# Anchor: [InDows:module] specialize-scripts
#
# NOTE: run STANDALONE (outside the GUI) this removes every app listed below. Through the InDows GUI you
# choose exactly which ones to remove; the safe, low-regret apps are pre-ticked, the rest are left to you.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-debloat-appx.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }
function Remove-App([string]$a) {
    Get-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -eq $a } |
        ForEach-Object { Remove-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online -PackageName $_.PackageName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null; Log "provisioned removed: $a" }
    Get-AppxPackage -AllUsers -Name $a -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        ForEach-Object { Remove-AppxPackage -Package $_.PackageFullName -AllUsers -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Log "installed removed: $a" }
}

Log '=== debloat-appx start ==='
# === start ===  (each line = one app the GUI can toggle)
Remove-App 'Microsoft.BingNews'                     # Bing News
Remove-App 'Microsoft.BingWeather'                  # MSN Weather (the taskbar weather widget is unaffected)
Remove-App 'Microsoft.BingSearch'                   # web results in the Start-menu search box

Remove-App 'Microsoft.PowerAutomateDesktop'         # Power Automate (desktop flows)
Remove-App 'Microsoft.GamingApp'                    # Xbox app = the Game Pass client (KEEP if you use Game Pass)

tweaks.label: Brave Rewards / BAT off
tweaks.description: Turns off Brave Rewards, the built-in system that pays you BAT crypto tokens for viewing ads. When on, the Rewards feature and its toolbar icon are gone. Applied as a managed policy, so Brave shows 'managed by your organization'.

tweaks.label: Brave Wallet off
tweaks.description: Disables Brave's built-in crypto Wallet. When on, the Wallet panel and its icon no longer appear. Applied as a managed policy (Brave shows 'managed by your organization').

tweaks.label: Brave VPN off
tweaks.description: Disables Brave's paid built-in VPN. When on, the VPN button and its option disappear from the browser. Applied as a managed policy (Brave shows 'managed by your organization').

tweaks.label: Leo AI chat off
tweaks.description: Turns off Leo, Brave's built-in AI chat assistant. When on, the Leo panel and its sidebar/address-bar entry are removed. Applied as a managed policy (Brave shows 'managed by your organization').

tweaks.label: Usage stats ping off
tweaks.description: Stops Brave sending its daily 'still active' usage ping to Brave's servers (used to count active users). Nothing changes visually, there is just less telemetry. Applied as a managed policy (Brave shows 'managed by your organization').

tweaks.label: Brave News off
tweaks.description: Turns off Brave News, the scrollable news feed on the new-tab page. When on, that feed no longer loads. Applied as a managed policy (Brave shows 'managed by your organization').

tweaks.label: Brave Talk off
tweaks.description: Disables Brave Talk, the built-in video-calling feature. When on, the Brave Talk widget on the new-tab page and its menu option are removed. Applied as a managed policy (Brave shows 'managed by your organization').

tweaks.label: Private Tor windows off
tweaks.description: Removes the 'New private window with Tor' option that routes browsing through the Tor anonymity network. When on, only ordinary private windows remain available. Applied as a managed policy (Brave shows 'managed by your organization').

tweaks.label: Privacy-preserving analytics off
tweaks.description: Turns off P3A, Brave's anonymous, privacy-preserving analytics that report aggregate feature usage. Nothing changes visually, Brave just stops sending that data. Applied as a managed policy (Brave shows 'managed by your organization').

tweaks.label: Anonymized URL data collection off
tweaks.description: Stops Brave sending anonymised data tied to the web addresses you visit (used to improve its features). Nothing changes visually, there is just less telemetry. Applied as a managed policy (Brave shows 'managed by your organization').

tweaks.label: Extended safe-browsing reports off
tweaks.description: Stops Brave sending Google detailed reports about suspicious pages you visit. Normal Safe Browsing protection stays fully on, only the extra detailed telemetry is turned off. Applied as a managed policy (Brave shows 'managed by your organization').

tweaks.label: Metrics reporting off
tweaks.description: Turns off sending general usage and diagnostic metrics to Brave. Nothing changes visually, there is just less telemetry. Applied as a managed policy (Brave shows 'managed by your organization').

modules.name: developer-tools
modules.description: Opt-in developer conveniences (off by default): `sudo` in force-new-window mode + Developer Mode (sideload / run unsigned trusted apps).
modules.why: Handy for developers: run elevated commands with sudo, and sideload / run your own unsigned apps.

modules.content:
# InDows module: developer-tools
# Opt-in developer conveniences: `sudo` (force-new-window mode) + Developer Mode. OFF by default.
# Anchor: [InDows:module] specialize-scripts
#
# These lower a few guardrails on purpose (sideloading, elevation). Turn on only what you need.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-developer-tools.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }

    New-Item -Path $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null

Log '=== developer-tools start ==='

tweaks.description: Enables the Windows 'sudo' command so you can run a command with admin rights from an ordinary terminal. It uses the safer 'new window' mode, meaning the elevated command opens in a separate window rather than inside your current one.

modules.content:
# InDows module: disable-ai
# Turns off Windows AI features, machine-wide. Each line is independent -- comment out what you want to keep.
# Runs elevated during the "specialize" pass. Anchor: [InDows:module] specialize-scripts

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-disable-ai.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }

    New-Item -Path $path -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $path -Name $name -Value $val -PropertyType DWord -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
}
$ai = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsAI'

Log '=== disable-ai start ==='
# Windows Copilot
RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsCopilot' 'TurnOffWindowsCopilot' 1
# Recall: "AI data analysis" + saved screen snapshots
RegDword $ai 'DisableAIDataAnalysis' 1
RegDword $ai 'TurnOffSavingSnapshots' 1
# Click to Do (the "act on what's on screen" feature)
RegDword $ai 'DisableClickToDo' 1
# Microsoft Edge: hide the Copilot/Discover sidebar
RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge' 'HubsSidebarEnabled' 0
RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge' 'ShowSidebarButton' 0

# --- optional (commented) ---
# Generative AI features inside Edge (Compose, etc.):
# RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge' 'GenAILocalFoundationalModelSettings' 1
# The taskbar Copilot BUTTON is a per-user setting -> put it in a default-user tweak if you want it hidden
# for new users: ...\Explorer\Advanced\ShowCopilotButton = 0

tweaks.description: Turns off Windows Copilot, the built-in AI assistant. When on, the Copilot button and its side panel no longer open.

tweaks.label: Recall: "AI data analysis" + saved screen snapshots
tweaks.description: Turns off Recall, the feature that periodically saves snapshots of your screen so AI can search your past activity. When on, no screen snapshots are taken or analysed.

modules.name: disk
modules.description: **Automatic disk wipe + standard UEFI layout on disk 0** (EFI + MSR + NTFS C:). Replaces the interactive disk step.
modules.why: Replaces the interactive disk step with a fully automatic wipe + standard UEFI layout on disk 0.
modules.riskNote: DESTRUCTIVE: it ERASES disk 0 with no confirmation. Be certain which drive is disk 0 (unplug other disks if unsure). Data loss is permanent.
modules.content:
<!-- ============================================================================
     InDows module: disk  (automated disk layout)
     Replaces the INTERACTIVE disk step with a fully automatic wipe + standard UEFI
     layout on DISK 0. The base leaves disk selection interactive; add this only if
     you want zero clicks AND you are sure which disk is "disk 0".

     WHERE: settings pass="windowsPE" > component "Microsoft-Windows-Setup"
            (add BOTH the <DiskConfiguration> and the <ImageInstall> below)

     **** DANGER ****  WillWipeDisk = true ERASES disk 0 with no confirmation.
     Make sure disk 0 is the target drive (unplug other disks if unsure).
     ============================================================================ -->
<DiskConfiguration>
    <Disk wcm:action="add">
        <DiskID>0</DiskID>
        <WillWipeDisk>true</WillWipeDisk>
        <CreatePartitions>
            <CreatePartition wcm:action="add">
                <Order>1</Order>
                <Type>EFI</Type>
                <Size>300</Size>
            </CreatePartition>
            <CreatePartition wcm:action="add">
                <Order>2</Order>
                <Type>MSR</Type>
                <Size>16</Size>
            </CreatePartition>
            <CreatePartition wcm:action="add">
                <Order>3</Order>
                <Type>Primary</Type>
                <Extend>true</Extend>
            </CreatePartition>
        </CreatePartitions>
        <ModifyPartitions>
            <ModifyPartition wcm:action="add">
                <Order>1</Order>
                <PartitionID>1</PartitionID>
                <Format>FAT32</Format>
                <Label>System</Label>
            </ModifyPartition>
            <ModifyPartition wcm:action="add">
                <Order>2</Order>
                <PartitionID>3</PartitionID>
                <Format>NTFS</Format>
                <Label>Windows</Label>
                <Letter>C</Letter>
            </ModifyPartition>
        </ModifyPartitions>
    </Disk>
</DiskConfiguration>
<ImageInstall>
    <OSImage>
        <InstallTo>
            <DiskID>0</DiskID>
            <PartitionID>3</PartitionID>
        </InstallTo>
    </OSImage>
</ImageInstall>

modules.name: explorer-ui
modules.description: Show file extensions, show hidden files, open to This PC, hide Home/Gallery, drive-letters-first, hide duplicate
modules.why: Makes File Explorer show extensions, hidden files and open to This PC — the sane defaults power users expect.

tweaks.label: Show known file extensions
tweaks.description: Makes File Explorer show file extensions. When on, filenames appear with their type visible, for example 'report.pdf' instead of just 'report'.

tweaks.label: Show hidden files

tweaks.label: Open Explorer to This PC (not Home)
tweaks.description: Makes new File Explorer windows open to 'This PC' rather than the 'Home' view. When on, Explorer starts on your drives and folders instead of a recent-files feed.

tweaks.label: Show drive letter before the label
tweaks.description: Puts the drive letter before the drive name. When on, drives read like 'C: Windows' instead of 'Windows (C:)'.

tweaks.label: Auto-expand the nav pane to the open folder
tweaks.description: Makes the left navigation pane automatically unfold to reveal the folder you currently have open. When on, the folder tree expands to show exactly where you are.

tweaks.label: Hide Gallery in the nav pane
tweaks.description: Removes the 'Gallery' photo-timeline entry from Explorer's left navigation pane. When on, Gallery no longer appears in the sidebar.

tweaks.label: Compact mode (tighter row spacing)
tweaks.description: Turns on compact view, which tightens the spacing between rows. When on, more files and folders fit on screen with less padding around each one.

tweaks.label: Show protected operating-system files
tweaks.description: Also reveals protected operating-system files, which stay hidden even with 'show hidden files' on. When on, critical system files become visible, handy for troubleshooting but easy to edit or delete the wrong thing.

tweaks.label: Hide Home in the nav pane (leaves This PC)
tweaks.description: Removes the 'Home' entry from Explorer's navigation pane, leaving This PC. When on, the Home shortcut disappears from the sidebar.

tweaks.label: Show empty drives
tweaks.description: Shows drives even when they have no disc or card inserted, such as an empty card reader or DVD drive. When on, those empty drives still appear under This PC.

tweaks.label: Show the full path in the title bar

modules.name: gaming
modules.description: GameDVR / background recording off (`GameDVR_Enabled=0`, policy `AllowGameDVR=0`), Game Mode, mouse acceleration
modules.why: Tunes Windows for games: Game Mode on, GameDVR recording off, no mouse acceleration.
modules.riskNote: Fullscreen Optimizations and HAGS are GPU/driver-dependent — they can help or hurt depending on your hardware.
modules.content:
# InDows module: gaming
# Background recording (GameDVR) OFF, Game Mode ON, mouse acceleration OFF.
# Runs during specialize WITH the default-user hive loaded. Anchor: [InDows:module] default-user-scripts
# (It also writes one machine-wide policy; that's fine from this anchor too.)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-gaming.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }
function RegDword([string]$p, [string]$n, [int]$v) {
    New-Item -Path $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name $n -Value $v -PropertyType DWord -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
}
function RegString([string]$p, [string]$n, [string]$v) {
    New-Item -Path $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name $n -Value $v -PropertyType String -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
}
$U = 'Registry::HKEY_USERS\DefaultUser'

Log '=== gaming start ==='
# GameDVR / background recording OFF (machine policy + per-user)
RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\GameDVR' 'AllowGameDVR' 0
RegDword "$U\System\GameConfigStore" 'GameDVR_Enabled' 0
RegDword "$U\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\GameDVR" 'AppCaptureEnabled' 0
# Game Mode ON
RegDword "$U\Software\Microsoft\GameBar" 'AutoGameModeEnabled' 1
# Mouse acceleration OFF (these three are REG_SZ)
RegString "$U\Control Panel\Mouse" 'MouseSpeed' '0'
RegString "$U\Control Panel\Mouse" 'MouseThreshold1' '0'
RegString "$U\Control Panel\Mouse" 'MouseThreshold2' '0'

# --- ADVANCED (commented) - DRIVER-DEPENDENT: these can help OR hurt depending on your GPU + driver + game ---
# Fullscreen Optimizations OFF (force true exclusive fullscreen; can lower latency, can also break HDR/capture):
# RegDword "$U\System\GameConfigStore" 'GameDVR_FSEBehaviorMode' 2
# RegDword "$U\System\GameConfigStore" 'GameDVR_FSEBehavior' 2
# Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS) ON (good on recent GPUs, problematic on some older/driver combos):
# RegDword 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\GraphicsDrivers' 'HwSchMode' 2
Log '=== gaming done ==='

tweaks.label: GameDVR / background recording OFF (machine policy + per-user)
tweaks.description: Turns off the background game recording used by Xbox Game Bar (Game DVR). When on, Windows no longer records your gameplay in the background, which can free up performance while you play.

tweaks.label: Game Mode ON
tweaks.description: Turns on Game Mode, which tells Windows to prioritise the running game and hold back background activity. When on, the active game gets first call on system resources.

tweaks.label: Mouse acceleration OFF
tweaks.content:
RegString "$U\Control Panel\Mouse" 'MouseSpeed' '0'
RegString "$U\Control Panel\Mouse" 'MouseThreshold1' '0'
RegString "$U\Control Panel\Mouse" 'MouseThreshold2' '0'
tweaks.description: Turns off mouse acceleration ('enhance pointer precision'), so the pointer moves the same distance no matter how fast you flick the mouse. When on, aiming becomes consistent and 1:1, which most gamers prefer.

modules.name: gpu-tuning
modules.description: Vendor power-state tweaks under `{4d36e968-…}\NNNN` (index known only **after** driver install → first-logon).
modules.why: Vendor GPU power-state tweaks (NVIDIA/AMD/Intel) that can cut micro-stutter on some cards.

modules.name: locale-keyboard

modules.why: Sets your language and keyboard layout during install, so you don't pick them by hand at OOBE.
modules.riskNote: Standard install setting. A wrong layout is fixed in Settings in seconds.
modules.content:
<!-- ============================================================================
     InDows module: locale-keyboard
     Sets language, region (formats) and keyboard layout automatically, so the
     first-run language/keyboard screens are skipped.

     WHERE: settings pass="oobeSystem" - ADD this whole component.
     ANCHOR (a comment in the base) named:   [InDows:module] oobe-international

</component>

modules.name: misc
modules.description: RTC-as-UTC for dual-boot ([S] 🟢), verbose logon, long paths, NumLock at boot, restore point (**post-install**, not
modules.why: A grab-bag of small fixes: RTC-as-UTC for dual-boot, long-path support, NumLock at boot, the classic photo viewer.
modules.riskNote: Small, well-understood tweaks. The restore point is created post-install, not during.
modules.content:

# Small machine-wide quality-of-life tweaks. Anchor: [InDows:module] specialize-scripts
# Each is independent -- comment out the ones you don't want.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'

    New-Item -Path $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null

tweaks.label: RTC kept in UTC -> no clock fight with a Linux dual-boot. (Only useful if you dual-boot Linux.)
tweaks.description: Tells Windows to read the PC's hardware clock as UTC instead of local time. When on, Windows and a Linux dual-boot stop overwriting each other's clock, so the time no longer jumps by your timezone offset after switching operating systems. Only useful if you dual-boot Linux.

tweaks.label: Allow long file paths (> 260 characters)
tweaks.description: Removes the old 260-character limit on file and folder paths. When on, apps that support it can create and open files with very long path names without errors.

tweaks.label: NumLock ON at the logon screen (.DEFAULT = the sign-in profile; for your own session it follows your last state)
tweaks.description: Turns NumLock on at the sign-in screen. When on, the numeric keypad types digits straight away, so you can enter a numeric PIN or password without pressing NumLock first.

tweaks.label: Verbose "Starting Windows / Signing out..." status messages instead of the spinner
tweaks.description: Shows detailed status messages such as 'Starting Windows' and 'Signing out' during boot and sign-out. When on, you see what Windows is actually doing instead of just a spinning circle.

modules.name: network-dns
modules.description: Set DNS (presets: Cloudflare, Google, Quad9, OpenDNS, AdGuard + family/malware variants, IPv4+IPv6), disable
modules.why: Points DNS at a fast, private resolver (Cloudflare, Quad9…) instead of your ISP's, for speed and privacy.
modules.riskNote: Reversible. If the resolver is ever down, switch back to automatic DNS.
modules.content:
# InDows module: network-dns
# Sets DNS servers on every active physical adapter. Runs at FIRST LOGON (needs a live network).
# Anchor: [InDows:module] first-logon-scripts
# Pick a provider by editing $dns below (uncomment one). Default = Cloudflare.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-network-dns.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }

$dns = @('1.1.1.1', '1.0.0.1')   # [InDows:param DNS] Cloudflare (default; the InDows GUI can pick another below)
# $dns = @('1.1.1.2', '1.0.0.2')               # Cloudflare (malware blocking)
# $dns = @('9.9.9.9', '149.112.112.112')       # Quad9
# $dns = @('94.140.14.14', '94.140.15.15')     # AdGuard
# $dns = @('8.8.8.8', '8.8.4.4')               # Google
# $dns = @('208.67.222.222', '208.67.220.220') # OpenDNS

Log "=== network-dns start (servers: $($dns -join ', ')) ==="
Get-NetAdapter -Physical -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq 'Up' } | ForEach-Object {
    try {
        Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceIndex $_.ifIndex -ServerAddresses $dns -ErrorAction Stop
        Log "  set DNS on '$($_.Name)'"
    } catch { Log "  FAILED on '$($_.Name)': $_" }
}
Log '=== network-dns done ==='

modules.name: network-profile
modules.description: Set the active network to the Private profile (`Set-NetConnectionProfile -NetworkCategory Private`) so LAN discovery/sharing works.
modules.why: Private lets file/printer sharing and device discovery work on your home network; Public locks them down.
modules.riskNote: Only do this on a network you trust (home/office), never on public Wi-Fi.

modules.name: optional-features
modules.description: Enable/disable via DISM: Hyper-V, WSL, Windows Sandbox, .NET 3.5, NFS, legacy media (WMP/DirectPlay), OpenSSH Server,
modules.why: Turns on Windows features (Hyper-V, WSL, Sandbox, .NET 3.5…) you want up front — tick them one by one; all start off.
modules.riskNote: Additive: nothing is enabled unless you tick it. Hyper-V and Windows Sandbox need Windows Pro/Enterprise and a reboot; Hyper-V can also clash with third-party VM software (VMware/VirtualBox) and some game anti-cheat.

tweaks.label: Hyper-V (Pro only)
tweaks.description: Turns on Hyper-V, Windows' built-in virtualization for running virtual machines. Needs Windows Pro/Enterprise and a reboot. It can conflict with some third-party hypervisors (VMware/VirtualBox) and certain game anti-cheat.

tweaks.label: Windows Subsystem for Linux
tweaks.description: Turns on the Windows Subsystem for Linux (the legacy component) so you can run Linux distributions. The newer winget 'Microsoft.WSL' app is the modern alternative.

tweaks.label: Virtual Machine Platform (WSL2)
tweaks.description: Turns on Virtual Machine Platform, the low-level component WSL2 and sandbox features rely on.

tweaks.label: Windows Sandbox (Pro only)
tweaks.description: Turns on Windows Sandbox, a throwaway isolated desktop for safely testing untrusted apps. Needs Windows Pro/Enterprise and a reboot.

tweaks.label: .NET Framework 3.5
tweaks.description: Turns on .NET Framework 3.5, which some older apps still need. It may require the Windows install media or an internet connection to finish.

modules.name: performance
modules.why: Nudges scheduling, multimedia and input latency toward responsiveness on a desktop.
modules.riskNote: Background-apps-off and single-svchost trade some convenience and RAM behaviour — measurable, not magic.
modules.content:
# InDows module: performance
# Foreground-responsiveness + multimedia scheduler tweaks. Machine-wide, specialize pass.
# Anchor: [InDows:module] specialize-scripts

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-performance.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }
function RegDword([string]$p, [string]$n, [int]$v) {
    New-Item -Path $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name $n -Value $v -PropertyType DWord -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
}
function RegString([string]$p, [string]$n, [string]$v) {
    New-Item -Path $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name $n -Value $v -PropertyType String -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
}

Log '=== performance start ==='
# Favor foreground apps (short, variable quantum with foreground boost)
RegDword 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\PriorityControl' 'Win32PrioritySeparation' 38
# Multimedia System Profile
$mm = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Multimedia\SystemProfile'
RegDword $mm 'SystemResponsiveness' 10
RegDword $mm 'NetworkThrottlingIndex' ([int]-1)   # -1 = 0xFFFFFFFF = network throttling off
# Per-task scheduling for games
$g = "$mm\Tasks\Games"
RegDword  $g 'GPU Priority' 8
RegDword  $g 'Priority' 6
RegString $g 'Scheduling Category' 'High'
RegString $g 'SFIO Priority' 'High'

# --- ADVANCED (commented) - bigger hammer, weigh it ---
# Force a SINGLE svchost process (less service isolation; set the value to your RAM in KB --
# 8 GB = 8388608, 16 GB = 16777216, 32 GB = 33554432):
# RegDword 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control' 'SvcHostSplitThresholdInKB' 16777216
# (Per-user perf tweaks -- background apps off, keyboard repeat speed -- belong in [U] modules.)
Log '=== performance done ==='

tweaks.label: Favor foreground apps (short, variable quantum with foreground boost)
tweaks.description: Tunes the CPU scheduler to give more attention to whatever app is in front. When on, the window you're actively using gets a larger share of processor time, which can make it feel more responsive.

tweaks.label: Multimedia System Profile
tweaks.description: Reduces how much CPU Windows holds back for background system tasks, leaving more for media and games. When on, foreground playback and games get a bit more processor headroom.

tweaks.label: Network throttling off
tweaks.description: Removes the network throttle Windows applies to protect audio and video playback. When on, network-heavy apps and downloads can use the connection's full speed.

tweaks.label: Per-task scheduling for games
tweaks.content:
RegDword  $g 'GPU Priority' 8
RegDword  $g 'Priority' 6
RegString $g 'Scheduling Category' 'High'
RegString $g 'SFIO Priority' 'High'
tweaks.description: Raises the CPU, GPU and disk priority Windows gives to programs it recognises as games. When on, games are scheduled ahead of ordinary background tasks.

modules.name: power
modules.description: Hibernate + Fast Startup off (`powercfg /h off`), Ultimate Performance plan (`powercfg -duplicatescheme e9a42b02…`),
modules.why: Disables hibernate / Fast Startup and enables the Ultimate Performance plan for a snappier, cleaner-shutdown desktop.
modules.riskNote: Power-throttling and USB-power-saving off drain more on a laptop — leave them on for a portable machine.
modules.content:
# InDows module: power
# Turns Hibernate + Fast Startup OFF and activates the "Ultimate Performance" power plan.
# Anchor: [InDows:module] first-logon-scripts  (powercfg is most reliable in a live session)
#
# NOTE (laptops): hibernate off removes the hiberfile and Fast Startup. "Ultimate Performance" keeps the
# CPU/devices at full power -> great on a desktop, worse battery on a laptop.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-power.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }

Log '=== power start ==='
# Hibernate off (also disables Fast Startup, which relies on the hiberfile)
& powercfg.exe /hibernate off
New-Item -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Power' -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null

# InDows module: privacy-telemetry

modules.riskNote: Opens an inbound network service. Only enable it on a machine and network you control — reach RDP over a VPN or a trusted LAN, never expose it straight to the internet.
modules.content:
# InDows module: remote-desktop
# Turns on Remote Desktop (RDP) so you can connect to this PC from another machine.
# Network Level Authentication stays ON (the secure default). Anchor: [InDows:module] specialize-scripts

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-remote-desktop.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }

Log '=== remote-desktop start ==='

reg.exe add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server" /v fDenyTSConnections /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

What does break: 'microsoft-edge:' links (some Start/search and notification links) and the default PDF/HTML handler, which you must reassign. modules.name: security
modules.description: Default (🟡): BitLocker auto-encryption off. **Danger zone (commented out, opt-in 🔴)**: lower UAC, disable SmartScreen,
modules.why: Turns off BitLocker auto-encryption by default; a commented "danger zone" can lower UAC or disable SmartScreen/Defender.
modules.riskNote: The danger-zone options genuinely reduce security — opt in knowingly (they're commented out, so you enable them by hand). This lowers protection but won't damage the OS or hardware. Defender can't be disabled while Tamper Protection is on.
modules.content:
# InDows module: security
#
# DEFAULT (active): stop AUTOMATIC BitLocker device encryption (defensible - avoids surprise lockout).
#
# OPTIONAL "danger zone" (commented out below): tweaks that LOWER your protection. They are commented on
# purpose so you cannot enable them by accident. Read each warning, then uncomment ONLY what you
# understand and accept. Anchor: [InDows:module] specialize-scripts

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-security.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }
function RegDword([string]$p, [string]$n, [int]$v) {
    New-Item -Path $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name $n -Value $v -PropertyType DWord -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
}
function RegString([string]$p, [string]$n, [string]$v) {
    New-Item -Path $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name $n -Value $v -PropertyType String -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
}

Log '=== security start ==='

# ---- DEFAULT (safe): prevent automatic BitLocker device encryption ----
RegDword 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\BitLocker' 'PreventDeviceEncryption' 1
Log 'PreventDeviceEncryption = 1 (automatic BitLocker off)'

# ============================================================================
#   ##############  DANGER ZONE  ##############
#   Everything below LOWERS your security. ALL of it is disabled (commented).
#   Uncomment a block ONLY if you fully understand and accept the consequences.
#   Don't do this just because a video told you it makes the PC "faster".
# ============================================================================

# --- Lower / disable UAC ----------------------------------------------------
#   RISK: programs can elevate to admin WITHOUT asking you. Malware then runs with full rights silently.
#   Option A (softer): never show the admin consent prompt, UAC engine stays on.
# RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System' 'ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin' 0
#   Option B (nuclear): fully disable UAC. Also breaks Store/UWP apps and some Settings pages.
# RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System' 'EnableLUA' 0
# Log 'UAC lowered (DANGER)'

# --- Disable SmartScreen ----------------------------------------------------
#   RISK: Windows stops warning you about malicious / unknown downloads, apps and websites.
# RegString 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer' 'SmartScreenEnabled' 'Off'
# RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System' 'EnableSmartScreen' 0
# RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge' 'SmartScreenEnabled' 0
# Log 'SmartScreen disabled (DANGER)'

# --- Microsoft Defender (GRANULAR - pick exactly what you turn off) ----------
#   Some people want Defender fully gone; others just want to drop cloud/sample sharing but KEEP real-time
#   scanning. Uncomment only the pieces you want off.
#   NOTE: all of these are IGNORED while Tamper Protection is ON (the default). To make them stick you must
#   first disable Tamper Protection by hand in Windows Security. InDows does NOT bypass it.
#
#   (a) Cloud-delivered protection off (keeps local real-time scanning):
# RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Spynet' 'SpynetReporting' 0
#   (b) Automatic sample submission off (2 = never send):
# RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Spynet' 'SubmitSamplesConsent' 2
#   (c) Real-time monitoring off (still installed, just not scanning live):
# RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Real-Time Protection' 'DisableRealtimeMonitoring' 1
#   (d) THE WHOLE ENGINE off (nuclear - no antivirus at all):
# RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender' 'DisableAntiSpyware' 1
# Log 'Defender tweaks applied (only effective if Tamper Protection was already off) (DANGER)'

Log '=== security done ==='

tweaks.label: Prevent automatic BitLocker encryption
tweaks.description: Stops Windows silently turning on BitLocker device encryption during setup. Prevents a surprise 'enter your recovery key' lockout on a PC you didn't mean to encrypt. This is the safe default.

tweaks.label: UAC: never show the admin consent prompt
tweaks.description: Stops User Account Control ever asking for confirmation when a program wants admin rights — it just silently allows it. The UAC engine stays on, but you lose the 'are you sure?' prompt, so malware can elevate without you noticing. Lowers your security.

tweaks.label: UAC: fully disable (nuclear)
tweaks.description: Fully turns off User Account Control: programs get full admin rights with no prompt at all. It also breaks many Store/UWP apps and some Settings pages. Strongly discouraged.

tweaks.label: Disable SmartScreen
tweaks.description: Turns off SmartScreen, so Windows and Edge stop warning you about malicious or unknown downloads, apps and websites. You lose a key layer of malware protection.

tweaks.label: Defender: cloud-delivered protection off
tweaks.description: Stops Microsoft Defender sending suspicious files to Microsoft's cloud for a faster verdict. Local real-time scanning stays on, but brand-new threats are caught a bit slower. (Ignored while Tamper Protection is on.)

tweaks.label: Defender: automatic sample submission off
tweaks.description: Stops Defender automatically uploading sample files to Microsoft — a privacy trade-off that slightly weakens cloud detection. (Ignored while Tamper Protection is on.)

tweaks.label: Defender: real-time monitoring off
tweaks.description: Turns off Defender's live scanning, so files are no longer checked as they're opened or run. Defender stays installed but is not actively protecting you. (Ignored while Tamper Protection is on.)

tweaks.label: Defender: disable the whole engine (nuclear)
tweaks.description: Disables the Microsoft Defender antivirus engine entirely — the PC then has no built-in antivirus. Only do this if you run another antivirus. (Ignored while Tamper Protection is on; you must turn that off by hand first.)

modules.name: services-tune
modules.description: Two presets:
modules.why: Sets rarely-used services to Manual to trim background load; a hardening preset goes further.
modules.riskNote: The hardening preset can break remote management or connectivity if mis-set — it's an opt-in allow-list.
modules.content:
# InDows module: services-tune
# Sets services to Manual (or Disabled in the hardening preset). Anchor: [InDows:module] specialize-scripts
#
# Choose a preset:
#   'safe'      -> rarely-used services to Manual (they still start on demand). Zero risk.
#   'hardening' -> also disables some telemetry/remote services (advanced; read the warnings).
# Edit the lists to taste -- each name is a service. Find names with: Get-Service | Sort Name

$preset = 'safe'   # [InDows:param PRESET] the InDows GUI can switch this to 'hardening'

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-services-tune.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }

# --- SAFE: rarely needed on a personal desktop -> Manual (start on demand) ---
$toManual = @(
    'MapsBroker'        # Downloaded Maps Manager
    'Fax'               # Fax
    'RetailDemo'        # Retail Demo (store kiosks)
    'WMPNetworkSvc'     # Windows Media Player network sharing
    'PhoneSvc'          # Phone Service
    'WalletService'     # Wallet
    'lfsvc'             # Geolocation
    'SCardSvr'          # Smart Card (uncomment-worthy only if you use smart cards)
    'WbioSrvc'          # Windows Biometric (only if no fingerprint/face login)
    'TabletInputService' # Touch Keyboard & Handwriting (desktop without touch)
)
$toDisabled = @()

if ($preset -eq 'hardening') {
    # --- ADVANCED: telemetry + remote-management. ---
    # WARN: don't disable RemoteRegistry / WinRM (RemoteAccess) if you manage this PC remotely.
    # NEVER add Dhcp / Dnscache / NlaSvc / WlanSvc here -- that breaks networking.
    $toDisabled += @(
        'DiagTrack'         # Connected User Experiences and Telemetry
        'dmwappushservice'  # WAP Push message routing (telemetry)
        'RemoteRegistry'    # remote registry access
        'RetailDemo'
        'WerSvc'            # Windows Error Reporting
    )
    $toManual += @('SysMain')   # SysMain/Superfetch (some prefer it Manual on SSD)
}

Log "=== services-tune start (preset: $preset) ==="
foreach ($s in ($toManual   | Select-Object -Unique)) { Set-Service -Name $s -StartupType Manual   -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Log "  Manual:   $s" }
foreach ($s in ($toDisabled | Select-Object -Unique)) { Set-Service -Name $s -StartupType Disabled -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Log "  Disabled: $s" }
Log '=== services-tune done ==='

modules.name: storage-sense
modules.description: Enable Storage Sense + auto-clean Recycle Bin (60 d) and Downloads not opened in 60 d (`StorageSense\Parameters\StoragePolicy`).
modules.why: Keeps disk space in check automatically instead of letting trash and old downloads pile up.
modules.riskNote: It auto-deletes old Recycle Bin and Downloads files after the number of days you set (default 60) — don't keep things long-term in Downloads.
modules.content:
# InDows module: storage-sense
# Turn on Storage Sense: auto-clean the Recycle Bin (60 days) and Downloads not opened in 60 days.
# Anchor: [InDows:module] default-user-scripts

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'

function RegDword([string]$p, [string]$n, [int]$v) {
    New-Item -Path $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null

}
$sp = 'Registry::HKEY_USERS\DefaultUser\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\StorageSense\Parameters\StoragePolicy'

modules.name: timezone
modules.description: Identity the base leaves interactive; these automate it. XML snippets (see each module folder).
modules.why: Sets the time zone during install, so the clock is right from first boot.
modules.riskNote: Trivial and reversible in Settings.
modules.content:
<!-- ============================================================================
     InDows module: timezone
     Sets the time zone automatically. Without it, Windows uses the region picked
     during the first-run setup.

     WHERE: settings pass="specialize" > component "Microsoft-Windows-Shell-Setup"
     ANCHOR (a comment in the base) named:   [InDows:module] specialize-shell-setup

     REPLACE: __TIMEZONE__  with a Windows time-zone ID (NOT a city/offset).
       List them with:   tzutil /l        (or  Get-TimeZone -ListAvailable )
       Examples: "Romance Standard Time" (FR/CET), "GMT Standard Time" (UK),
                 "Pacific Standard Time", "Eastern Standard Time", "UTC"
     ============================================================================ -->
<TimeZone>__TIMEZONE__</TimeZone>

modules.name: username
modules.description: Identity the base leaves interactive; these automate it. XML snippets (see each module folder).
modules.why: Creates your local account during install, so you skip the Microsoft-account nag at OOBE. Pick Administrator or a standard (non-admin) account.
modules.riskNote: The password is stored in clear text in the answer file. Pair with autologon only if you accept that. A standard account is safer for day-to-day use.
modules.content:
<!-- ============================================================================
     InDows module: username
     Creates a local user account automatically, so the first-run "create account"
     screen is skipped. Without this module the base leaves that screen interactive.

     WHERE: settings pass="oobeSystem" > component "Microsoft-Windows-Shell-Setup"
     ANCHOR (a comment in the base) named:   [InDows:module] account

     REPLACE before use:
       __USERNAME__   the account name (e.g. Alex)
       __PASSWORD__   the password, in PLAIN TEXT
                      -> for NO password, use an empty value: <Value></Value>
       __GROUP__      Administrators (admin) or Users (standard, non-admin)

     SECURITY: the password is stored in clear text in autounattend.xml.
     Never commit a real password to a public repo. Keep your filled-in file local.
     ============================================================================ -->
<UserAccounts>
    <LocalAccounts>
        <LocalAccount wcm:action="add">
            <Name>__USERNAME__</Name>
            <DisplayName>__USERNAME__</DisplayName>
            <Group>__GROUP__</Group>
            <Password>
                <Value>__PASSWORD__</Value>
                <PlainText>true</PlainText>
            </Password>
        </LocalAccount>
    </LocalAccounts>
</UserAccounts>

params.label: Password (leave blank for none; stored in clear text)

modules.name: visual-effects
modules.description: Dark mode, disable transparency/animations, `MenuShowDelay=0`, `StartupDelayInMSec=0`, "adjust for best performance"
modules.why: Drops transparency and animations and adjusts for best performance — a faster-feeling UI.
modules.riskNote: Cosmetic. Toggle animations back in Settings if you miss them.
modules.content:
# InDows module: visual-effects
# Snappier visuals for new users. Each line is independent -- comment out anything you want to KEEP.
# Anchor: [InDows:module] default-user-scripts

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-visual-effects.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }
function RegDword([string]$p, [string]$n, [int]$v) {
    New-Item -Path $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name $n -Value $v -PropertyType DWord -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
}
function RegString([string]$p, [string]$n, [string]$v) {
    New-Item -Path $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name $n -Value $v -PropertyType String -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
}
$U = 'Registry::HKEY_USERS\DefaultUser'

Log '=== visual-effects start ==='
# --- individual tweaks (active) ---
RegDword  "$U\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize" 'EnableTransparency' 0    # no transparency
RegDword  "$U\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced" 'TaskbarAnimations' 0      # no taskbar animations
RegString "$U\Control Panel\Desktop" 'MenuShowDelay' '0'                                              # instant menus
RegString "$U\Control Panel\Desktop\WindowMetrics" 'MinAnimate' '0'                                   # no minimize/maximize animation
RegDword  "$U\Software\Microsoft\Windows\DWM" 'EnableAeroPeek' 0                                      # no "peek at desktop"
RegDword  "$U\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Serialize" 'StartupDelayInMSec' 0    # no Start menu startup delay
RegDword  "$U\Control Panel\Accessibility" 'DynamicScrollbars' 0                                      # always show scrollbars (no auto-hide)
RegDword  "$U\Software\Microsoft\Clipboard" 'EnableClipboardHistory' 1                                # clipboard history (Win+V)

# --- NUCLEAR option (commented): "adjust for best performance" turns off basically ALL effects (plainer look) ---
# RegDword "$U\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\VisualEffects" 'VisualFXSetting' 2
Log '=== visual-effects done ==='

tweaks.label: No transparency
tweaks.description: Turns off the transparency and blur effects on the taskbar, Start menu and other surfaces. When on, those surfaces become solid, which can feel a touch faster.

tweaks.label: No taskbar animations
tweaks.description: Turns off the small taskbar animations. When on, taskbar buttons appear and disappear instantly instead of sliding.

tweaks.label: Instant menus
tweaks.description: Removes the built-in delay before menus open. When on, right-click menus and submenus pop up instantly instead of after a short pause.

tweaks.label: No minimize/maximize animation
tweaks.description: Turns off the animation when you minimise or maximise a window. When on, windows snap open and closed instantly instead of zooming.

tweaks.label: No "peek at desktop"
tweaks.description: Turns off Aero Peek, which previews the desktop when you hover the far-right corner of the taskbar. When on, hovering there no longer makes your windows go transparent.

tweaks.label: No Start menu startup delay
tweaks.description: Removes the deliberate delay Windows adds before launching your startup apps after sign-in. When on, startup programs load immediately instead of after a pause.

tweaks.label: Always show scrollbars (no auto-hide)
tweaks.description: Keeps scrollbars permanently visible instead of hiding them until you hover. When on, scrollbars stay as a solid, easy-to-grab bar at all times.

tweaks.label: Clipboard history (Win+V)
tweaks.description: Turns on clipboard history. When on, pressing Win+V shows a list of the last several things you copied so you can paste any one of them back.

modules.name: wallpaper
modules.description: Set the desktop + lock-screen image (you stage the image first). reg [HKCU] + Personalization CSP.
modules.why: Sets the desktop and lock-screen image for new users (you stage the image first).
modules.riskNote: Cosmetic. Needs the image file present, or it falls back to the default.
modules.content:
# InDows module: wallpaper
# Sets the desktop wallpaper and (optionally) the lock-screen image. Anchor: [InDows:module] first-logon-scripts
# Put your image(s) on the disk first (see README), then set the paths below. Leave a path empty to skip it.

$desktop = '__WALLPAPER__'    # your desktop image (the InDows GUI fills this; e.g. C:\Path\to\img.jpg)
$lock    = '__LOCKSCREEN__'   # your lock-screen image (optional)
$style   = '10'   # fit mode: 10 = Fill, 6 = Fit, 2 = Stretch, 0 = Center, 22 = Span

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-wallpaper.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }

Log '=== wallpaper start ==='
if ($desktop -and (Test-Path $desktop)) {
    Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Control Panel\Desktop' -Name 'WallPaper' -Value $desktop -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Control Panel\Desktop' -Name 'WallpaperStyle' -Value $style -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Start-Process -FilePath 'rundll32.exe' -ArgumentList 'user32.dll,UpdatePerUserSystemParameters' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Log "desktop -> $desktop (style $style)"
} elseif ($desktop) { Log "desktop image not found: $desktop" }

if ($lock -and (Test-Path $lock)) {
    $csp = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\PolicyManager\current\device\Personalization'
    New-Item -Path $csp -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    Set-ItemProperty -Path $csp -Name 'LockScreenImagePath'   -Value $lock -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Set-ItemProperty -Path $csp -Name 'LockScreenImageUrl'    -Value $lock -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Set-ItemProperty -Path $csp -Name 'LockScreenImageStatus' -Value 1     -Type DWord -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Log "lockscreen -> $lock"
}
Log '=== wallpaper done ==='

modules.name: wifi
modules.description: Join a Wi-Fi network at first logon (WPA2-Personal; cleartext password). `netsh wlan`.
modules.why: Joins a Wi-Fi network at first logon, so a wireless-only PC is online without manual setup.
modules.riskNote: Stores the Wi-Fi password in clear text in the config. Treat the media as a secret.
modules.content:
# InDows module: wifi
# Joins a Wi-Fi network at first logon (handy when there's no Ethernet). Anchor: [InDows:module] first-logon-scripts
# Edit $ssid / $password below. WPA2-Personal (the common home setup).
# SECURITY: the password is in clear text here -> keep this file local.

$ssid     = '__SSID__'
$password = '__PASSWORD__'

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-wifi.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }

Log "=== wifi start (SSID: $ssid) ==="
$wlanXml = @"
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<WLANProfile xmlns="http://www.microsoft.com/networking/WLAN/profile/v1">
  <name>$ssid</name>
  <SSIDConfig><SSID><name>$ssid</name></SSID></SSIDConfig>
  <connectionType>ESS</connectionType>
  <connectionMode>auto</connectionMode>
  <MSM><security>
    <authEncryption><authentication>WPA2PSK</authentication><encryption>AES</encryption><useOneX>false</useOneX></authEncryption>
    <sharedKey><keyType>passPhrase</keyType><protected>false</protected><keyMaterial>$password</keyMaterial></sharedKey>
  </security></MSM>
</WLANProfile>
"@
$tmp = "$env:TEMP\InDows-wifi-profile.xml"
$wlanXml | Out-File -FilePath $tmp -Encoding ascii
& netsh.exe wlan add profile filename="$tmp" user=all *>> $log
& netsh.exe wlan connect name="$ssid" *>> $log
Remove-Item -LiteralPath $tmp -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Log '=== wifi done ==='

params.label: Wi-Fi password (WPA2; stored in clear text)

modules.name: windows-update
modules.description: Delivery Optimization off, pause auto-reboot while active, defer feature updates, active hours. reg (HKLM policy).
modules.why: Tames Windows Update: no forced reboots while you're active, Delivery Optimization off, feature updates deferred.
modules.riskNote: Deliberately does not disable updates — keeping the OS patched is the "don't break Windows" line.
modules.content:
# InDows module: windows-update
# Tame Windows Update WITHOUT disabling it: no peer-to-peer downloads, no auto-reboot while you're using
# the PC. Anchor: [InDows:module] specialize-scripts

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$log = 'C:\Windows\Temp\InDows-windows-update.log'
function Log([string]$m) { "{0}  {1}" -f (Get-Date -Format 'o'), $m | Add-Content -Path $log }
function RegDword([string]$p, [string]$n, [int]$v) {
    New-Item -Path $p -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    New-ItemProperty -Path $p -Name $n -Value $v -PropertyType DWord -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
}

Log '=== windows-update start ==='
# Delivery Optimization: download from Microsoft only (0 = no LAN/Internet peer sharing)
RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeliveryOptimization' 'DODownloadMode' 0
# Never auto-reboot while a user is signed in
RegDword 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU' 'NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers' 1
Log '=== windows-update done ==='

tweaks.label: Delivery Optimization: download from Microsoft only (0 = no LAN/Internet peer sharing)
tweaks.description: Turns off peer-to-peer update sharing, so updates download only from Microsoft rather than from or to other PCs on your network or the internet. When on, your PC also stops uploading update files to other machines.

tweaks.label: Never auto-reboot while a user is signed in
tweaks.description: Stops Windows Update from automatically restarting the PC while someone is signed in. When on, updates wait for you to restart yourself instead of forcing a reboot in the middle of your work.
